verdict: As a tired judge this one would make me lean forward: it is the only entry likely to ship the ★★★ problem end-to-end, the visual IS the algorithm (incumbents streamed from the worker, van positions from the same projectState the re-planner uses), and the first number on screen is checked against a published optimum, which no other PS on the sheet allows. Must-haves 1–3 are met literally as written, no watch-out is violated (time budgets 2 s/5 s are visible; OR-Tools scaling is moot and explained), and the honesty plan (eval-frozen tag before tuning, dev/test instance split, iteration-budget determinism, refused-order-with-reason) is better than anything I expect from the other 29 teams. But two things I verified tonight would sink the demo exactly as scripted: (1) the headline "gap 0.0%" is unreachable under the idea's stated distance convention. I recomputed the committed C101.sol on disk: double precision gives 828.937, per-arc truncation to one decimal gives exactly 827.3; and the same three routes restricted to customers ≤25 give 191.814 (double) vs 191.3 (truncated) = SINTEF's C101.25 optimum. So the 25-customer SINTEF/Kohl values use per-arc floor(10·d)/10, and the idea's "double precision reported to one decimal" would print 191.8 vs 191.3 (+0.27%) with the provably optimal route, and nobody on the team could explain why. (2) The scripted "+5 orders at t=110, four stitched in, one refused" is contradicted by the actual R101 file (fetched from the iRB-Lab mirror): customers 26–30 have windows [132,142], [37,47], [39,49], [63,73], [71,81]; four of the five had closed 30–70 time units before injection. With hard windows four are refused, with the proposed soft windows (λ=2, π=1000) all four get served absurdly late because 2×~150 < 1000, and the judge who reads the tooltip sees it. Also, R101.25 is the wrong demo instance for the breakdown: with 8 vans/25 customers and 10-wide windows, at t=90 only 14 stops remain pending across 8 vans (1–2 per van, max 3), so the "4 remaining stops turn amber" moment cannot happen and the fleet barely re-organises; RC101.25 (4 vans, 19 pending stops at t=90, 30-wide windows) gives the drama the script promises. All three are hour-zero fixes, not design flaws, which is why this is a 7.5 as written and an 8.5–9 if the fixes land before the eval-frozen tag.
fatal_flaws: Distance convention mismatch on the headline number (verified): SINTEF's 25-customer optima (Kohl et al.) sum per-arc distances truncated to one decimal. Evidence computed tonight from the files on disk with C:\Users\anand\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-anand-AppData-Roaming-Claude-scratch-workspaces-6d3f6ae3-a9cf-43a1-9f02-084f51aa24ce-94af3f7e-8586-428b-8d2f-3ab2c2e6953c-scratch-2026-10-21-ad7c8b\e663623e-d0f9-4c19-bbe9-186e28591477\scratchpad\conv_check.py: C101.sol = 828.937 (double) / 827.3 (trunc1); C101.25 subset routes [5 3 7 8 10 11 9 6 4 2 1], [13 17 18 19 15 16 14 12], [20 24 25 23 22 21] = 191.814 (double) / 191.3 (trunc1). The idea's stated convention guarantees a non-zero gap on an optimal route and an unanswerable Q&A. Fix: in benchmark mode build the Float64Array matrix as Math.floor(10*d)/10 per arc, print 'convention: truncated to 0.1 (Kohl et al. 1999 / DIMACS)' next to the badge, keep a double-precision toggle for operational mode, and add a vitest that the three C101.25 routes above evaluate to exactly 191.3.

Scripted new-order outcome contradicts the real data (verified from the iRB-Lab R101.txt): customers 26–30 of R101 have windows [132,142], [37,47], [39,49], [63,73], [71,81]. Injected at t=110, 27/28/29/30 are already dead; with λ=2 and π=1000 the solver will serve them 60–150 units late instead of dropping them (lateness penalty < drop penalty), so the map shows vans delivering to expired windows and the 'one honestly refused' line is false. Fix: select the 5 new orders by rule 'ready_time ≥ t_inject + 5' from the parent instance and print the rule in the UI (for R101 at t=110 the candidates are 26[132–142], 34[117–127], 46[117–127], 50[124–134], 56[130–140], 32, 43, 55, 37, 66, 96, 97); let refusal emerge from the solver, never from pre-expired windows; apply the same rule for RC101/C101 parents.

Wrong demo instance for the breakdown: on R101.25 at t=90 only 14 stops have due > 90 (ids 1,3,4,6,8,9,10,13,17,18,20,22,24,25) spread over 8 vans, so a van has 1–2 pending stops (3 at most, e.g. 18→6→13 chain) and the promised '4 remaining stops turn amber' and visible fleet re-organisation cannot occur; R101.25's 8 vans for 25 customers also leave so much slack that the disruption cost is near zero. Fix: make RC101.25 (4 vans, 19 pending stops at t=90, 30-unit windows, BKS 4/461.1) the scripted demo scenario (breakdown of the van with the most pending stops, shown in the van picker), keep R101.25 and C101.25 in the benchmark table; verify tonight with the bench script that the chosen seed yields ≥3 orphans, ≥1 late delivery and a visible reassignment, and label it 'chosen for legibility' as planned.
weaknesses: Objective mismatch: the 25-customer SINTEF optima minimise total distance; the idea's 10000·K + D (vehicles-first) can legitimately find fewer vehicles with longer distance on some instances and then print a positive 'gap' against an incomparable number, confusing the comparison the badge exists to make.

No strong-baseline comparison in core: a judge who wrote 'suggested stack: OR-Tools' will ask 'what does OR-Tools get in 5 s on the same instances?' and the answer is currently a stretch goal. BKS alone shows how far you are from optimal, not whether the hand-rolled ALNS beats the tool you declined to use.

The repair-vs-full-re-solve race is foregone on 25-customer instances: full re-solve on ~15 free stops converges to near-optimal in 2 s every time, so the 'winner badge' always says Full and the stretch-goal comparison carries no information; the trade-off only becomes real at 100 customers.

Demo script is 305 s before judge hesitation, with 8 s of dead air on the 100-customer solve, a 40 s evidence segment that a tired judge will not read, and a timeline scrub that proves a point only engineers care about. Handing event buttons to a judge adds 10–20 s and a chance of the wrong button.

PathLayer getPath transitions only interpolate when vertex counts match; ALNS incumbents change route lengths every step, so 'routes untangle live' will mostly be opacity cross-fades (flicker) rather than the morph the script promises; 600 ms transitions overlapping 250 ms incumbent updates will also pile up.

The '2D map' is an abstract canvas; the PS says 'routes drawn on a 2D map' and suggests Leaflet. The honesty banner mitigates, but a literal judge may still say 'that is a scatter plot'; Plotly (also suggested) would be equally abstract, so this is survivable but should be pre-empted in one sentence.

PS lists 'backend APIs' as a skill and the entry has zero backend; the worker protocol answer is fine, but 'how would a real fleet call this?' needs a one-line demonstrable answer rather than a shrug.

Unstated state-model rules that a sharp judge will probe: what a van that has not yet departed does (re-plannable from depot at its planned departure?), whether a van that returned to depot can be re-dispatched for new orders, and whether orphans are required (must-have 2 says 'reassigning the broken van's remaining stops', so orphans must never be droppable; only new orders may be prize-collecting). The idea implies but does not state this.

'~600 lines' of solver is not credible for I1 + 4 destroy + 3 repair + SA + adaptive weights + precedence-aware joint insertion + prize-collecting + soft windows + virtual starts; expect 1,200–1,600 lines. Claiming 600 and showing 1,500 reads as spin; the explainability argument should rest on docs/solver.md and named module owners, not a line count.
First commit at 21:50 leaves a 3h50m gap after kickoff with hourly commits required 'from kickoff'; a planning-only DEV_LOG entry explains it, but the gap is avoidable.

Rescue-node precedence is modelled as 'any route serving an orphan must visit R_b first'; an orphan whose parcel could simply be reloaded at the depot by a van that has not yet departed is forced through the breakdown point. Minor and defensible as an assumption, but it should be written down.

Soft windows only after the disruption: a judge can say 'late deliveries appear only because you relaxed the rules'. The formulation is right (a dead van makes hard windows infeasible) but the KPI panel should make that reasoning visible.
fixes: evaluate.ts: benchmark mode uses per-arc floor(10·d)/10 (matches 191.3/827.3 exactly, verified); operational mode double precision; the badge prints the convention; vitest asserts the three C101.25 routes evaluate to 191.3 and the committed C101.sol to 827.3.
static.ts: benchmark objective = total distance (the Kohl et al. objective), vehicles reported alongside; vehicles-first only as an operational toggle; the README says why in one sentence.

events.ts: new orders chosen by rule ready ≥ t_inject + 5 from the parent file (for R101@110: 26, 34, 46, 50, 56), rule printed in the tooltip; refusal must come from the solver; scenarios.json regenerated with this rule before the eval-frozen tag.

Demo scenario = RC101.25 with the breakdown of the van holding the most pending stops; verify tonight via bench that it yields ≥3 orphans and ≥1 late delivery; van picker shows pending-stop counts so a judge picks a juicy van.

Add an offline OR-Tools (×10 integer scaling, GLS, 5 s) or PyVRP 0.14.1 column to bench/results_static.csv as core, not stretch: ~30 minutes of Python run once on a laptop, committed with the command; it answers 'why not OR-Tools' and shows the ALNS is competitive against the suggested tool under the same budget.

Run bench/run_dynamic.ts on the 100-customer trio as well (10 seeds) so repair-vs-full has a real trade-off to report; on 25-customer instances report it honestly as 'full re-solve always wins quality in 2 s; repair wins on stability and time'.

Resample every route path to a fixed vertex count (e.g. 48 points along the polyline) keyed by vehicle index so PathLayer getPath transitions always interpolate; set transition 200 ms to match the 250 ms incumbent cadence; throttle incumbent application to 4 Hz.

Demo script cuts: drop the timeline scrub (10 s), pre-solve the 100-customer instance in a background worker while the evidence tab is open and show only the finished gap (saves 15 s), evidence segment = one sentence plus one highlighted row (25 s), driver QR moves to the closing slide; operator presses Solve/Play, judge is offered only the Breakdown button; total target 270 s.

Ship one file api/replan.ts (Vercel serverless, same src/core import, 10 s cap) that returns a plan for a POSTed reduced problem, never used in the demo; it is the one-line answer to 'backend APIs' and 'how would a real fleet call this'.

docs/replan.md and the UI banner state the five state-model rules explicitly: served stops frozen; in-service stop completes; mid-arc vans interpolate; not-yet-departed vans re-plan from the depot at max(t, planned departure); returned vans are done; orphans are required stops (never dropped), only new orders are prize-collecting.
KPI tile 'late deliveries' shows a sub-line 'would be infeasible under hard windows: N stops' so the soft-window switch reads as measurement, not relaxation.
Commit the README skeleton, LICENSE, .env.example and DEV_LOG (with the honest 18:00–21:30 planning entry) immediately, not at 21:50.
Rewrite the explainability claim as 'five files, one-page pseudo-code, named owner per file' and drop the '600 lines' number.

Add one sentence to the pitch and the banner pre-empting the map question: 'Solomon instances are abstract coordinates; a geographic basemap would imply a city that does not exist, so we draw a synthetic grid and say so.'

Q&A card deck must include: distance convention (now answerable), why distance-only objective in benchmark mode, OR-Tools comparison numbers, why new orders have those ids, what breaks it (asymmetric real-road times, >200 stops in a browser tab), and where the AI is (adaptive operator selection is an online bandit; the track is explicitly OR).
steal_worthy: External-truth badge: the first number on screen is compared to a published optimum with its convention and source printed next to it; any entry with a known baseline should open this way.
Streaming incumbents from a Web Worker every 250 ms so 'watch it think' is literally the solver's trajectory, not an animation.
One projectState(plan, t) shared by renderer and re-planner so a state-model bug is visible on the map instead of hidden in a log.
eval-frozen git tag committing scenarios/test sets before any tuning, with iteration budgets for determinism and time budgets only in interactive mode (and the UI saying which is in use).
Copy-scenario-link (instance, seed, event sequence URL-encoded) so a judge can reproduce an exact demo run on their own laptop.
Refused-order-with-reason pattern ('not served: window closes t=142, nearest van ETA t=151') with the penalty slider visible, which turns 'orders not served' from a failure into a design decision.
Zero-backend static deployment with workers as the compute tier: no cold start, no API keys, no Wi-Fi dependency, demo-proof by construction.
The 'race' panel (two strategies, two workers, convergence curves, winner badge, show-alternative overlay) as a general way to demo any heuristic-vs-exact or fast-vs-thorough comparison.
